sections.html:
Enterprise is a city in southeast Alabama, mostly in Coffee County with a western slice of Dale County, in the Wiregrass region. The 2020 census counted 28,711 residents, and the city sits right outside Fort Rucker, the home of Army Aviation.

The city covers about 31 square miles at an elevation near 305 feet. It is the principal city of the Enterprise micropolitan area, which the Census Bureau now treats separately from nearby Dothan.

sections.h2: Why is there a boll weevil statue in Enterprise?
sections.html:
The Boll Weevil Monument in the middle of Main Street honors the insect that forced local farmers to try new crops. John Henry Carmichael settled the site in 1881 and opened a store, the city incorporated in 1896, and the Alabama Midland Railway arrived soon after.

In 1915, boll weevils destroyed most of the cotton in Coffee County. Farmers planted peanuts and other crops, and within two years the county led the nation in peanut production. The monument was dedicated on December 11, 1919, and it is described as the only monument to an agricultural pest in the world.

A later art project called Weevil Way placed 30 decorated boll weevil statues around town at local landmarks and businesses.

sections.h2: What did the 2007 tornado do to Enterprise housing?
sections.html:
An EF4 tornado struck Enterprise on March 1, 2007, killing nine people and injuring more than 121. Damage was estimated at nearly $307 million, the worst disaster in the city's history.

A quarter-mile-wide swath through downtown was devastated, and at least 647 houses were damaged or destroyed. Eight of the deaths were students at Enterprise High School, which was rebuilt on a new site at the west end of Boll Weevil Circle and opened August 23, 2010, at a cost of over $80 million, with reinforced safe rooms.

After a storm like that, storm safety is a fair thing for a buyer to ask about. If your house was repaired after a storm, keep the permits and contractor paperwork, since a buyer or title company may ask for them.

Enterprise has added residents in every census since 1900, and the growth in the 2000s was steep: from 21,178 people in 2000 to 26,562 in 2010, a gain of 25.4 percent.

In 2020 about 25.5 percent of residents were under 18 and 15.6 percent were 65 or older, and 33.9 percent of households had children. Roughly 28 percent of households were one person living alone. Those figures describe a city with many families alongside a sizable group of older and single-person households, and both groups sell houses for reasons like downsizing, relocation or an estate.

When you describe your house to a buyer, state the year it was built and whether any part of it was rebuilt after a storm. That plain detail answers questions before they are asked.

sections.h2: What other weather affects Enterprise homes?
sections.html:
Enterprise has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild winters, moderated by its closeness to the Gulf Coast. It falls in USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 8B, and palm trees grow in town.

Hurricanes can reach this far inland. Wikipedia names Hurricane Eloise in 1975 and Hurricane Opal in 1995 as storms that caused extensive damage to the city, and it notes tornadoes can occur as well.

  • Roofs: age, missing shingles and tarps left from earlier storms.
  • Trees: any large limbs hanging over the roof or power lines.
  • Windows and doors: seals, storm shutters and previous water intrusion.
  • Insurance: any open claims or wind and hail deductibles that affect a sale.

Downtown Enterprise is built around the Boll Weevil Monument on Main Street, and the former Alabama Midland Railway depot now serves as the Depot Museum. The Enterprise Public Library holds a 1941 post office mural by Paul Theodore Arlt, saved when the old post office was torn down in 1991.

The city also hosted the BamaJam Music Festival, which drew as many as 100,000 people a night in its peak years, and it returned to BamaJam Farms in 2012 after a canceled 2011 show. Landmarks and events like these give the area a recognizable center, which helps when you explain to an out-of-town buyer where your house sits.

ZIP codes 36330 and 36331 cover the city, and the area code is 334. Mention both when you send a buyer a property description or run a title search.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and the college shape Enterprise?
sections.html:
U.S. 84 runs through the north side of the city along Boll Weevil Circle, heading northwest 16 miles to Elba and east 9 miles to Daleville. State Route 167 runs north and south along the east side of the circle, and State Routes 27 and 134 also pass through, with 134 running 26 miles west to Opp.

Enterprise City Schools serve the public school students, and Enterprise State Community College, a two-year school whose teams are the Boll Weevils, is in town. The Enterprise Ledger has covered local news since 1898.

The city's median age is 35.9, younger than Decatur or Dothan, and it has a college and an Army installation next door. If you own a rental, those two facts are worth mentioning to a buyer.

sections.h2: What is the process for selling a house in Enterprise?
sections.html:
A sale in Enterprise closes when the deed is recorded with the probate office of the county where the parcel lies, which is usually Coffee County and sometimes Dale County. Alabama charges a recordation tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, and a form attesting to the real purchase price goes with the deed, under section 40-22-1 of the state code.

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue.

  • Order a payoff letter if the house has a mortgage.
  • Find the deed and confirm every owner's name as it appears.
  • List any known repair problems so the buyer is not surprised.
  • Ask the closing agent how the current year's tax will be split.

sections.h2: What do Enterprise sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Enterprise grew from 26,562 people in 2010 to 28,711 in 2020, and some sellers here are working against a deadline. A set of orders, a new job or a family move can leave little time for showings.

  • Owners with a job transfer or relocation who need to close quickly.
  • Landlords whose tenants moved out and left damage.
  • Heirs who inherited a house and live elsewhere.
  • Owners of houses with older roofs, plumbing or heating and air systems.

A cash purchase can fit those situations because it can close on the seller's date and does not depend on a buyer's lender. Use the form on this page to describe your house and timing.

faqs.q: How many people live in Enterprise, Alabama?
faqs.a: Enterprise had 28,711 residents at the 2020 census. Most of the city is in Coffee County, with part in Dale County.

faqs.q: Is Enterprise close to Fort Rucker?
faqs.a: Yes. The city sits right outside Fort Rucker, the home of Army Aviation.

faqs.q: What tax is due when a deed is recorded in Enterprise?
faqs.a: Alabama's recordation tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value, paid before the deed is recorded. The closing agent normally collects it at closing.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Enterprise?
faqs.a: They are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Enterprise house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses with old roofs, storm wear or deferred maintenance sell for cash regularly, and you do not need to fix them first.
